title.en: Convex hull of a point cloud

summary: Build the hull of an editable point set and keep its degenerate outcomes visible instead of hiding them.
objective: Let me move points in space and watch the convex hull rebuild, including the cases where it collapses to a polygon, a segment or a point.
intent_signals: Show which points of a cloud are on the hull and which are inside.
Demonstrate what happens to a hull when all the points become coplanar.
example_prompts: Build an editable point cloud with its convex hull and a marker for interior points.
Show the degenerate hull cases when points are collinear or coplanar.
negative_signals: Not a mesh reconstruction tool: a hull is not a surface fit to concave data.
Not a collision engine, although the hull may be used as one input to one.
not_for: Not a mesh reconstruction tool: a hull is not a surface fit to concave data.
Not a collision engine, although the hull may be used as one input to one.

entities.name: Point set
entities.guidance: Give each point a stable ID and a draggable handle; hull membership is a computed property of the point, not a colour baked into it.

entities.name: Hull surface
entities.guidance: Build the hull as a closed set of planar facets with outward normals and shared edges, so it can be inspected face by face.

entities.name: Degenerate readout
entities.guidance: Display the current hull dimension in words as well as geometry, since a flat hull and a thin solid look alike from many angles.

state_contract.model: Point list with stable IDs and a hull recomputed after every edit, together with the affine dimension of the current point set (0 point, 1 segment, 2 planar polygon, 3 volumetric hull) and an explicit empty state. The recipe assumes an exact or clearly stated predicate strategy and does not claim numerical robustness by itself.
state_contract.authority: The point list is authoritative and the hull is always derived; no hull facet may persist after its supporting points move.
actions: Drag a point and watch the hull rebuild.
Collapse the set onto a plane and read the reported dimension.
Reset to the authored point set.
Remove points down to the empty set, which reports an empty hull instead of drawing one.

invariants: Every hull vertex is a point of the input set; the hull never invents a vertex.

Points are classified as extreme (hull vertices), non-extreme boundary points or strictly interior points. A point at the centre of a hull facet is a boundary point that is not a vertex, so a two-way extreme-versus-interior split is wrong.

The reported affine dimension drives what is drawn: collinear points give a segment, a single point or coincident points give a point, coplanar points give a planar polygon, and only dimension 3 has closed facets with outward normals.
motion_guidance: Rebuild the hull on release as well as during a drag, so the final state is never an interpolated intermediate.
Animate facet appearance and disappearance briefly; a facet that pops without explanation hides a topology change.
known_limits: Floating-point predicates can flip near-degenerate cases; robustness depends on the implementation you choose.
Hull complexity grows with the point count, and this recipe makes no interactive performance claim.

A documented hull routine can return a planar polygon with a border, so a returned polyhedron is not by itself evidence of a closed three-dimensional surface; the reported affine dimension is what decides.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: The convex hull of a set of points in three-dimensional space is a convex polytope whose vertices belong to that point set.
claims.scope: Definition as stated in the cited library documentation.

claims.statement: Degenerate inputs are expected: a documented hull routine may return a point, a segment, a triangle or a polyhedron depending on the configuration, and the non-degenerate variant assumes more than three points that are not all collinear.
claims.scope: Documented behaviour of one library version; your own implementation must state its own degenerate policy.

source_refs.locator: 3D Convex Hulls, degenerate cases and function variants

object_craft.structure: Small spheres with a size that stays legible at distance plus a ground-plane drop line so depth is readable.
object_craft.material: Three clearly separated materials for extreme, non-extreme boundary and strictly interior points, differing in value as well as hue so the classification survives greyscale viewing.
object_craft.articulation: Points translate under a drag handle constrained to a chosen plane or axis.

object_craft.structure: Flat facets with visible shared edges and consistent outward normals; no smoothing across facet boundaries.
object_craft.material: Semi-transparent facets over opaque edges so interior points remain visible through the hull.
object_craft.articulation: The surface is rebuilt, not deformed, whenever the point set changes.

physical_contract.scope: Geometric construction and presentation only; no dynamics or contact response.
checks: Every reported hull vertex ID exists in the point list.
Moving an interior point without leaving the hull does not change the facet set.
